title: "LINGUOPRAGMATIC CHARACTERISTICS OF ONOMATOPOEIC UNITS IN AUDIOVISUAL TRANSLATION: STRATEGIES FOR THEIR REPRESENTATION IN SUBTITLING AND DUBBING"
authors: Kayumova Ozoda Baxrom qizi; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This article examines the linguopragmatic characteristics of onomatopoeic units in audiovisual translation and analyzes the strategies used for their rendering in subtitling and dubbing. Onomatopoeic units, as expressive linguistic elements that imitate sounds of natural phenomena, objects, animals, and human actions, perform important semantic, pragmatic, and emotional functions in audiovisual discourse. Their translation requires not only the preservation of lexical meaning but also the accurate transmission of expressive effects, contextual relevance, and cultural connotations.

title: Sensor Data Transmission in Smart Agriculture: Challenges, Potentials, and Limitations in the Fourth Industrial Revolution
authors: Alvertos Ioannis Mourikis; Iosif Polenakis; Christos Sarantidis; Romanos Kalamatianos; Ioannis Karydis
abstract: Smart agriculture is a key application domain of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR), where cyber–physical systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), and data-driven analytics converge to improve productivity, sustainability, and resource efficiency. In this context, large volumes of sensor data collected in the field form the basis for automated monitoring, decision support, and adaptive control across agricultural processes. However, the value of such data depends not only on sensing technologies and connectivity, but also on how data are generated, transferred, processed, and interpreted throughout their lifecycle. This paper is organized in two parts. The first part reports a narrative review of the literature, based on a documented search protocol, and provides an overview of sensor data and sensor data transmission networks in smart agriculture. It examines the main challenges, potentials, and limitations associated with IoT-based field deployments in 4IR environments, and consolidates them into ten open problems. These problems are ordered from the device layer to the socio-economic layer and span physical robustness, device security, rural connectivity, aerial sensing, interoperability, labelled-data scarcity, explainability, federated access control, data ownership, and cost. The second part responds to these open problems with the conceptualization of a layered architecture and a set of design proposals, covering hierarchical edge security, offline-first synchronization, semantic interoperability, explainable decision support, and farmer-centric data governance, that are grounded in established techniques and standards but have not been implemented or empirically validated in this work; they are intended as a design blueprint and a starting point for future prototyping and evaluation rather than as measured results. The paper is accordingly positioned as a conceptual, perspective-oriented contribution: it states the procedure by which the open problems were derived from the reviewed works, it states what the proposed integration is claimed to add over existing smart-agriculture architectures, and it sets out an evaluation plan that fixes the metrics and the baselines against which each proposed component would have to be tested. Throughout both parts, particular attention is given to the role of data integrity and provenance as foundational elements for trustworthy agricultural data, enabling reliable analysis, auditability, and long-term reuse. By synthesizing current approaches, open issues, and conceptual solution patterns, this paper aims to support the design of resilient, transparent, and future-ready smart agriculture systems aligned with the principles of the 4IR.

title: SWT: Self-Supervised Video Object Segmentation via Sliding, Wavelet and Transportation
authors: Zhengtong Zhu; Jiaqing Fan; Hanwen Qian; Fanzhang Li
venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing Communications and Applications
abstract: Video Object Segmentation (VOS) aims to accurately segment target objects from consecutive video frames and track the changes of the objects in each frame of the video. Conventional VOS methods typically demand substantial quantities of pixel-level labeled video sequences for fully supervised learning, which limits the performance of the model in sparse video scenes, while existing VOS methods have limited adaptability to global changes in objects. Based on this observation, in this paper, we propose self-supervised VOS with Sliding window, Wavelet transform and optimal Transport (SWT), a self-supervised VOS framework entirely trained on static dataset using contrastive learning. Firstly, a rolling sample buffer reuses overlapping groups of independently sampled images across successive updates. Secondly, to address the long-distance modeling difficulty caused by simple convolutional structures, we introduce wavelet transform to expand the receptive field of convolutional kernels, thus improving the model's representational capability. Finally, we incorporate optimal transport to assist the model in finding the globally optimal match between the target across two frames, improving the model's ability to handle non-rigid deformations of objects. SWT only requires training on the COCO dataset once and achieves excellent results on five VOS datasets as well as an additional body part propagation dataset. The code will be released soon at https://github.com/machine928/SWT.git .

title: Health and Well-being
authors: Sławomir J. Ambroziak; Kamran Sayrafian
abstract: From smart wearables, implants, and ingestible electronics to remote physiological monitoring and public health, wireless technology has numerous applications in healthcare.It has the potential to create a pervasive environment for monitoring people's health and well-being while improving how physicians deliver care.It can also boost patient engagement and satisfaction by allowing them to spend more time in the comfort of their homes and interacting with their care centres whenever needed.The End-to-End (E2E) health data connectivity involves the development of technologies that enable reliable and location-agnostic communication between patients and healthcare service providers.The increasing penetration of connected devices in healthcare is a significant driver towards creating an intelligent network that enhances people's quality of life.In recent years, wearable biomedical sensors have experienced remarkable growth; however, there are still many societal challenges, including safety, security, interoperability, and integration with existing wireless infrastructure that need to be addressed.This chapter addresses various cutting-edge scientific problems dealing with communications inside or around the human body, novel antenna designs for wearables and implants, propagation channel characterisation, remote health monitoring, and innovative public health and safety applications.

title: UAV-based dynamic crowd monitoring for rescue prioritization using subspace-driven localization
authors: Zhitong Zhang; Mingliang Xiong; Wen Fang; Qingwei Jiang; Siyuan Du; Tianyi Lv
abstract: Abstract Rapid and reliable localization of survivors is critical in post-disaster search and rescue operations. However, conventional sensing methods such as visual imaging are often ineffective due to smoke, dust, or debris, and traditional RSSI-based localization suffers from severe multipath interference and noise. This paper proposes a subspace-driven multi-UAV system for dynamic crowd monitoring and rescue prioritization. The system employs Boustrophedon scanning to acquire spatially continuous RSSI sequences from survivors’ Wi-Fi devices. A spatial resampling technique is first applied to regularize the irregular measurements, followed by Hankel matrix construction and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to separate signal from noise, yielding robust coarse device locations. A multi-pass scanning strategy tracks devices over time, detects mobility as an indicator of vitality, and maintains device records with expiration mechanisms. Detected devices are mapped to predefined rescue zones, and a weighted priority score is computed for each zone based on device count, mobility, and temporal trends. Simulation results under low and high noise conditions demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms Kalman-filtered trilateration and SVD without resampling. At 6 dB noise, it achieves a 46.7% reduction in RMSE and a 60.0% reduction in outlier ratio. Furthermore, spatial resampling reduces computational time by 17% per device-line, with greater gains expected in high-frequency scenarios. The proposed framework transforms raw RSSI measurements into actionable intelligence for rescue command, enabling efficient resource allocation.

title: Telepresence and Teleoperation
authors: Nikhil Deshpande
abstract: This chapter elaborates on the handbook’s premise of establishing the notions of ergonomics and human factors in robotics, here in relation to the technologies of telepresence and teleoperation. As implemented through robotic systems, telepresence and teleoperation are often interchangeably used terms. Both use the prefix term “tele”, which pertains to communication over distance, and both refer to humans being able to do something—“being present” (telepresence) or “operating devices” (teleoperation)—at a distance. Semantically and technologically, telepresence and teleoperation exist by themselves, and one is not a necessary condition for the other. However, as technology has evolved, the interplay between the two has markedly increased. Nevertheless, humans, and their ability to interact with system elements, are central to both ideas. In that respect, ergonomics as a study of methods to optimise human well-being and improving overall system performance, must serve as an integral criterion in developing telepresence and teleoperation systems. The chapter details the idea of ergonomics in the domain of telepresence and teleoperation by tracing the evolution of telepresence and teleoperation, then illustrating the challenge of ergonomics and human factors engineering in this field, and further demonstrating how different aspects of this challenge can be addressed. The chapter concludes with a case study showing how the thread of ergonomics and human factors can be woven throughout the design and implementation of telepresence and teleoperation technologies, grounding them in human-centred arguments. The chapter aims to demonstrate how ergonomics principles fundamentally underpin the landscape of telepresence and teleoperation technologies. It lays the groundwork for advances in future telepresence and teleoperation systems that have ergonomics principles at their core.

title: Vision transformer-based generative auxiliary information from reconstructed video sequences
authors: Vladyslav Zakharchenko; Sebastian Schwarz
abstract: This paper investigates the generation of auxiliary depth pictures directly from reconstructed video sequences using Vision Transformer (ViT) foundation models. Unlike conventional immersive media systems that require explicit transmission of depth information, the proposed framework derives dense depth representations from decoded video pictures already available within the coding loop. A transformer-based depth estimation pipeline is applied to both original and reconstructed content to evaluate the robustness of depth derivation under video compression. Experimental results obtained using JVET AhG15 gaming-content datasets demonstrate that generated depth pictures preserve the dominant geometric structure of the scene across a wide range of coding conditions and exhibit strong resilience to compression artifacts. The results indicate that depth information can be treated as a recoverable latent representation that may be regenerated from reconstructed visual content rather than transmitted explicitly. This capability creates opportunities for geometry-aware rendering, semantic-assisted coding, synthesized reference generation, and machine-oriented video processing while reducing auxiliary-data transmission overhead. The proposed framework therefore provides a practical step toward future video coding architectures in which scene geometry is recovered directly from compressed video.

title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
authors: Weiliang Chen; Song Liao
abstract: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query-tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent.

title: Neurons++: A Unified Visual-Stream Framework for Image and Video Reconstruction from fMRI with Neural-to-Visual Interpretability
authors: Haonan Wang; Yuchen Wang; Jingyu Lu; Qixiang Zhang; Lehan Wang; Xuanqi Huang; Xiaomeng Li
abstract: Decoding visual experience from fMRI is important for understanding human perception and developing brain-computer interfaces. Recent generative decoding methods can reconstruct plausible images and videos, but visual plausibility alone does not ensure that the output is faithfully grounded in brain activity. In this work, we propose Neurons++, a visual-stream fMRI reconstruction framework for both static image and dynamic video reconstruction. Compared with our conference version Neurons, Neurons++ extends the paradigm from video-only reconstruction to visual-stream reconstruction for both images and videos, and replaces parallel task conditioning with serial cortex-inspired decoding. The model first uses image-fMRI pretraining to obtain a stable spatial-semantic initialization, and then performs subject-specific fine-tuning for image and video reconstruction separately. The serial design organizes fMRI-derived representations into explicit spatial, semantic, language-level, and temporal cues. Extensive experiments show that Neurons++ achieves state-of-the-art video reconstruction and competitive image reconstruction across standard benchmarks. Beyond reconstruction fidelity, neural-to-visual analyses indicate that Neurons++ exhibits qualitative directional controllability under neural perturbation, that its fMRI encoder read-out is sensitive to stimulus-relevant cortical features, and that it supports ROI-guided semantic modulation. Code and model weights are available at: https://github.com/xmed-lab/NeuronsPlusPlus.

title: Hidden Data Challenges in Clinical Machine Learning
authors: Carolin Cissée; Dennis Fast; Raneen Younis; Alexander Löser; Wolfgang Nejdl; Zahra Ahmadi
abstract: Widely reused preprocessing pipelines for electronic health records can encode assumptions about when information became available, what clinical episode a label represents, and what missingness means. These assumptions are rarely audited systematically and may propagate across subsequent studies when preprocessing pipelines are reused or adapted. Using MIMIC-IV as a case study, we identify and quantify violations of three complementary forms of preprocessing alignment, i.e., temporal, semantic, and population alignment, which manifest as temporal leakage, feature-task misalignment, and biased imputation. We show how ambiguities in timestamp semantics, episode definitions, endpoint construction, modality selection, and missingness handling can alter the information available to a model and affect the interpretation of its predictions. Through analyses of MIMIC-IV data and empirical case studies, we demonstrate that such choices may remain largely invisible in aggregate predictive performance while changing the signals on which models rely. We derive practical recommendations for temporally valid, clinically aligned, and reproducible preprocessing of MIMIC-IV and related electronic health record datasets. The code for our experiments, including our proposed preprocessing, is available at: https://github.com/m2l-lab/mimic-iv-preprocess.

title: CoVA: Composing VAE Representations for Generative Learning
authors: Zhaowei Chen; Yikai Ge; Linze Li; Yao Tang; Xiang Li
abstract: Representation alignment with pretrained visual encoders improves diffusion transformer training but requires auxiliary encoders and extra training overhead. Recent approaches instead exploit representations from the generative model's own variational autoencoder (VAE). However, reconstruction-oriented VAE features are not optimized for the semantic discrimination and spatial structure needed for generative learning. We introduce \textbf{CoVA} (\textbf{Co}mposed \textbf{VA}E Representations), a lightweight framework that composes VAE features online into stage-wise guidance for flow-matching training. A small latent composer is jointly trained with class supervision, masked latent reconstruction, and horizontal-flip consistency, yielding semantically discriminative, spatially structured dense features and sample-dependent class posteriors. CoVA aligns intermediate SiT features with the composed representations early in training, then removes the increasingly detrimental alignment and reuses detached composer posteriors for sample-dependent soft label conditioning. We further uncover a hidden confound in soft label conditioning: averaging class embeddings attenuates their magnitude, coupling semantic interpolation with conditioning strength. This attenuation alone can substantially improve FID while degrading Recall, revealing a non-semantic source of the apparent gain. CoVA corrects this confound by restoring the hard-label magnitude, isolating posterior-dependent directional semantics. CoVA adds only 8.5M training-only auxiliary parameters (1.3\% of SiT-XL/2) and introduces no inference-time overhead. On ImageNet 256$\times$256, CoVA reduces SiT-XL/2 FID from 17.2 to 7.4 (\textbf{57\%}) in 400K steps. With classifier-free guidance, it achieves an FID of \textbf{2.03} in only 400 epochs, versus 2.06 after 1,400 epochs for vanilla SiT-XL/2.

title: Vision Transformers Learn Word Meaning from Images Alone
authors: Anders Gjølbye; Sebastian Ray Mason; Stella Frank; Lars Kai Hansen
abstract: Can a vision model learn what words mean from pixels alone? We show that the two largest DINOv3 vision transformers organize words rendered in images by word meaning, despite being pretrained using self-supervision on images only, without paired captions, class labels, or other language supervision. We derive word representations from embedding differences between word images and matched controls, then test whether semantically related words are neighbors within each model's embedding space, while controlling for spelling similarity. We find that brand names in the same industry group together, as do nouns from the same semantic domain. Country-capital pairs exhibit consistent vector offsets, similarly to word embeddings trained on text. These word representations also align with the representations of the visual object categories they name. DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B are, to our knowledge, the first self-supervised vision models to show substantial semantic structure for rendered words. Comparisons with text and speech encoders reveal shared structure among representations of the same words. Contrastive alignment with either encoder further strengthened DINOv3-H's word-level semantic structure, while leaving the other finetuned vision models largely unchanged. Image-only training can therefore teach vision models not just what words look like, but also how their meanings relate.

title: Automated Detection and Encoding of Cartographic Signs in Historical Maps
authors: Remi Petitpierre
abstract: Symbols and icons in archival maps represent an expansive source of evidence for historical geography. In this paper, we present a two-stage framework for (1) detecting cartographic signs in historical maps and (2) generating interpretable sign embeddings that capture both semantics and stylistic variations. We also introduce CaSiDD, an open benchmark dataset spanning multiple sign categories and diverse cartographic styles, designed for generic sign detection. Using YOLOv10-X, we demonstrate the practicality of automated sign detection on historical maps. We then present strategies for creating contrasted, informative embeddings of cartographic signs. We approach embedding design systematically, maximizing expressiveness while suppressing digitization or background material confounders. Our final method, based on an adapted RADIOv4 backbone, effectively encodes both sign form and semantics, while producing interpretable representations. This work lays a foundation for scalable evidence extraction for the comparative study of map signs within cartographic culture and geohistorical research.

title: Destination-Conditioned Adaptation with Semantic-Geometric Alignment for Generative Inbetweening
authors: Zhiyu Xu; Wei Shang; Yushen Xu; Wenwen Li; Zhiyan Xu; Pengfei Zhu; Dongwei Ren
abstract: Generative inbetweening aims to synthesize temporally coherent intermediate frames between a start frame and a target frame. Although pretrained image-to-video diffusion models provide strong priors for large-motion inbetweening, they are not explicitly designed to reach a specified target frame. They may therefore generate realistic individual frames while drifting from the target or producing unstable motion under large displacements and non-rigid dynamics. We propose DSG-GI, a framework that adapts pretrained latent video diffusion models through \textbf{D}estination-Conditioned Adaptation and \textbf{S}emantic-\textbf{G}eometric Alignment. Destination-Conditioned Adaptation treats the target frame as the destination of the sequence and provides temporally progressive guidance along the generated trajectory. Semantic-Geometric Alignment aligns the token-wise spatio-temporal relational geometry of backbone features with that of a frozen video foundation encoder and applies a flow-matching-aware latent flow constraint to samples near the data endpoint of the probability path. Together, these components strengthen destination guidance and preserve coherent semantic-geometric motion structure. Extensive experiments on standard and large-motion inbetweening benchmarks demonstrate improvements in temporal stability, target-frame faithfulness, and perceptual quality. Our code will be made publicly available.

title: Robust Vision-Language Navigation with Awareness of Instruction-Execution Progress
authors: Jiagan Huang; Zikun Zhou; Hongpeng Wang; Guangming Lu; Jun Yu; Wenjie Pei
abstract: In Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) tasks involving multi-step instructions as guidance, an agent must associate its observations with the relevant instruction content at each decision point. Most graph-based methods commonly match candidate trajectories with the entire instruction, allowing already executed content to interfere with subsequent decisions. Although instruction-execution progress provides a direct cue for separating executed and pending content, existing progress estimation approaches often rely on explicit progress supervision, sophisticated progress-learning stages, or costly online reasoning with LLMs. In this paper, we propose a robust VLN framework with Awareness of Instruction-Execution Progress (VLN-AIEP), which couples progress estimation with navigation decision-making. VLN-AIEP associates the visited trajectory with the instruction to suppress embeddings corresponding to executed content, and then matches candidate locations with the pending content. This coupling makes correct navigation decisions depend on accurate progress estimation, allowing the progress estimator to learn directly from navigation decision labels without explicit progress annotations. To support progress estimation, we construct a landmark-anchored trajectory representation that encodes the semantic labels and viewpoint-relative geometry of instruction-referred landmarks. These landmarks serve as spatial references for associating the visited trajectory with executed instruction content. Extensive experiments on R2R, RxR, CVDN, and R2R-CE demonstrate that the proposed method achieves favorable performance across multiple metrics.

title: GeoGR: Spatial-Semantic Token Compression and Group Routing for Efficient 3D VLMs
authors: Yongxin Zheng; Hao Wu; Fang Li; Hu Fu; Peiran Yin; Xudong Wang; Haozhe Hu; Xinghao Chen; Yunpu Ma; Wei Zhang; Xiaoyu Shen
abstract: Multi-view representations enable pretrained image and video vision-language models to understand 3D scenes, but their long visual token sequences make inference costly. Redundancy arises both from repeated observations of the same scene regions across views and from processing all visual tokens at every LLM layer, regardless of their relevance to the current computation. We propose GeoGR, a two-stage framework that jointly compresses scene representations and visual computation. At the projector level, GeoSemZip consolidates cross-view observations into 3D voxel tokens and combines semantic saliency with spatial coverage to construct a compact scene representation. Unselected voxel features are aggregated into contextual anchors to retain scene information that would otherwise be discarded. At the LLM level, we identify an effective visual computation window and observe that query-conditioned token relevance remains locally stable but changes over longer layer intervals. Guided by these findings, GroupRoute combines late entry and early exit with recoverable group-wise skipping. Low-relevance tokens bypass complete LLM layers while retaining their hidden states and can rejoin the active group at subsequent anchor layers selected under a computation budget. For compression-aware post-training, we construct a compact dataset of 67K samples by retaining 30% of the original training pool. With this protocol, GeoGR retains 95.2% and 96.8% of the dense post-trained models' performance on LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Video-3D LLM-7B, respectively, while accelerating LLM prefill by $6.8\times$ and $6.1\times$. These results demonstrate the consistent effectiveness of GeoGR across 3D VLMs with and without explicit 3D spatial encoding, highlighting a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off. The code is available at https://github.com/EIT-NLP/GeoGR.

title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Finite-Beam Reachability and Continuous-Query Generation in Generative Recommendation
authors: Yu Sun; Renkai Xiang; Zuodong Xiang; Junwei Zhou; Yike Zhang; Jianxin Zhang; Zhihao Zhu; Xiaoyu Cao; Hailu Xu
abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) of social media platforms commonly retrieves items by autoregressively decoding discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) with finite-width beam search. This work examines how this output interface constrains whether held-out targets enter finite returned lists, while distinguishing catalog-wide scoreability from empirical top-K support. We introduce two continuous-query paradigms: CQG-Single generates one retrieval query in a single pass, and CQG-AR autoregressively generates continuous residual updates, retaining step-wise decoding while removing the SID item-token vocabulary, code lookup, and discrete beam expansion. These designs thereby eliminate the SID-specific reachability constraint induced by finite-beam decoding and avoid the technical challenge of aligning a discrete SID vocabulary with the pretrained backbone's vector space. Both methods make every encoded item directly scoreable through dense or approximate-nearest-neighbor retrieval. Under a unified protocol with valid-prefix constrained decoding, CQG-Single exceeds the TIGER-style baseline in all seven runs while using 55.3% as many trainable parameters. CQG-AR remains comparable on ML-1M and is numerically stronger on Beauty and Sports datasets. A controlled depth ablation further shows that additional continuous refinement does not monotonically improve shallow accuracy. These findings motivate decoupling output representation, autoregressive modeling, and retrieval budget when evaluating generative recommendation systems.

title: Towards Early and Accurate Disease Detection Through Multimodal Predictive Modeling: Fusion of Electronic Health Records, Medical Imaging, And Omics Data Using Interpretable Machine Learning.
authors: Muhammad Ahsan Hayat; Jahangir Baig; Shayan Ahmed; Ahmed Faraz Ayubi
abstract: Early detection of disease is a cornerstone for improving patient outcomes, reducing costs, and enabling preventative interventions. Traditional predictive models often rely on a single type of data (e.g., imaging, clinical labs, or genomics). However, human health is inherently multimodal, involving a variety of data sources such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable sensor data, genomics, and clinical notes. Integrating these heterogeneous modalities into unified predictive modelsoffers a path to richer, more accurate, and more robust disease detection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of methods in multimodal predictive modeling for early disease detection, illustrate architectural patterns and fusion strategies, discuss challenges (e.g. missing modalities, interpretability, generalizability, bias), and highlight promising directions. We also propose a reference architecture for developing such systems and suggest evaluation best practices.

title: Agentic code modernization
authors: Peter F. Peterson; Addi Malviya Thakur
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Software rots. Between refactors for new features, bug fixes, the continual march of cybersecurity advisories, and the slow drift of dependencies toward end-of-life, code must change or cease to exist. The simple act of keeping up can be overwhelming for research software engineers tasked with maintaining long-lived scientific codebases. To address this maintenance burden, the community has developed a vibrant ecosystem of language- and framework-specific tools, such as Dependabot for dependency bumps [1], Clang-Tidy for C++ static analysis [2], and Python Refurb for idiom modernization [3], alongside a host of similar utilities. These tools, while monumental in their contribution, are necessarily limited in scope: they encode a fixed catalog of transformations, they tend to operate on a single file or a single dependency at a time, and they presumably cannot reason about the broader architectural or semantic consequences of a change. More recently, agentic AI systems have arrived. Unlike single-shot code completion, agentic systems can read across a repository, run tests, observe failures, and iterate, and these behaviors, in principle, may enable a different class of modernization task. In this talk, we present concrete examples of modernizing Mantid [4], a more than 20-year-old C++ and Python project with roughly two million lines of code. We attempted to leverage agentic AI to perform maintenance work and modernization work on research software. Changes proposed by the agents were validated against the project's existing automated test suite and reviewed by human maintainers before merging. By exploring successes and failures, the presentation will improve attendees' understanding of when, and with what guardrails, to use AI to assist in modernizing their code. References Dependabot. title: A Disease-Memory Guided Framework for Radiology Report Generation from Multi-View Chest X-rays
authors: Prajakta Dhamanskar; Chintan Bhupeshbhai Thacker; Saurabh A Shah
venue: Journal of Electronics Electromedical Engineering and Medical Informatics
abstract: Chest X-rays are widely used, low-cost diagnostic tools. Writing chest X-ray reports manually is a time-consuming and tedious task. The increasing number of X-rays burdens radiologists, creating a need for a clinically accurate, fast and automated report generation system. To solve this challenge, we propose a new disease-memory-guided vision-language framework for radiology report generation. Frontal and lateral chest X-rays (multi-view) are encoded using a Swin-Transformer. These encoded visual features are then passed through a multi-label classification head that predicts disease probabilities, from which the top three labels are converted into learnable disease-memory embeddings. These are concatenated with projected visual tokens and fixed task instruction embeddings to form a multimodal prompt which is fed into a frozen decoder. A LLaMA-2-7B model adapted to the radiology domain using LoRA fine-tuning on the train-only MIMIC-CXR subset is used as an autoregressive decoder. The disease-memory embeddings serve as disease guidance during report generation. An extensive experimental analysis of different experimental variants is conducted on the benchmark Indiana University Chest X-ray dataset using three aspects: 1) statistical n-gram overlap, 2) semantic similarity, and 3) clinical label-based metrics. Experimental results of the proposed system show improvements in semantic evaluation metrics, with BERTScore precision, recall, and F1 values of 0.898, 0.891 and 0.894, respectively, and ROUGE-L and METEOR scores of 0.327 and 0.281, indicating improved contextual consistency between generated and reference reports. However, performance on statistical metrics (e.g., BLEU4=0.068) and clinical evaluation metrics remains limited, with Micro-F1, Macro-F1, Precision and Recall values of 0.4211, 0.0640, 0.4272, and 0.4151, respectively, indicating only partial abnormality description. This framework improves abnormality grounding while maintaining computational efficiency and can be used as a supportive tool for preliminary report drafting in research or resource-constrained settings.

title: BASG: A Behavior-Augmented Semantic Generalization Framework for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation
authors: Zihao Pan; Peilun Li; Yue Li
abstract: Training sequential recommenders for interaction-disjoint target domains is challenging: no target interaction data are available for training, model selection, or calibration. Semantic item representations support transfer across non-overlapping catalogs but do not encode query-local temporal signals or interaction-derived properties such as popularity and co-occurrence. We propose BASG (Behavior-Augmented Semantic Generalization), a backbone-compatible framework combining a source-trained semantic scorer with a separately trained Behavior Expert via a common candidate-score interface. The expert integrates query-local temporal features with popularity- and co-occurrence-related proxies predicted from frozen item-text embeddings by source-fitted mappers. Static Fusion standardizes and combines the two score vectors using a source-selected coefficient fixed during target evaluation. Catalog-level text representations and transferred property proxies are precomputed offline and reused at inference, without target-side calibration or aggregate target-domain statistics. Across three semantic backbones and three target domains including the cross-platform Steam dataset, BASG improves mean NDCG@10 by 0.43–1.68 percentage points in all nine backbone–target settings. In SAGERec-based analyses on the two Amazon targets, the interaction-property channel shows the larger removal effect, while source-calibrated Static Fusion transfers more reliably than the tested source-trained routers. These results support BASG as a strategy for integrating transferable behavioral evidence under a strict zero-shot protocol.

title: LEXICO-SEMANTIC AND COGNITIVE CHARACTERISTICS OF MOTION LEXEMES
authors: Sarsenbayev H.A.; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The article investigates the lexico-semantic and cognitive characteristics of motion lexemes through a comparative analysis of the English and Karakalpak languages. Motion lexemes form a comprehensive semantic group that encodes not only spatial displacement but also properties like manner, speed, direction, and path. The study employs componential analysis, frame semantics, and conceptual metaphor theory to examine the structural features, semantic asymmetry, and prototypical organization of these lexical units. It highlights that the conceptualization of motion is shaped by human perception, physical experience, and typological constraints, such as the distinction between satellite-framed and verb-framed language structures.

title: AMHCNet: an Adaptive Multi-Scale Heat Conduction Network for Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
authors: Yu Shen; Dong Shi; Sheng Xu
abstract: Remote sensing image semantic segmentation is challenging due to complex spatial structures. However, existing methods often struggle to fully exploit hierarchical contextual information, leading to limited segmentation performance. To alleviate this, we propose AMHCNet, an Adaptive Multi-Scale Heat Conduction Network, to enhance hierarchical feature representation and contextual propagation for remote sensing image semantic segmentation. The network contains two key components: a Scale-Specific Heat Conduction (SSHC) module that applies heat conduction with scale-dependent strength to each encoder stage, and an Adaptive Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (AMFF) module that dynamically fuses heat-enhanced features with adaptive weights. SSHC captures both local details and long-range semantic context, while AMFF preserves fine structures and aggregates global information. Extensive experiments on ISPRS Potsdam and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate that AMHCNet achieves better performance compared with several state-of-the-art methods while maintaining competitive computational efficiency.

title: Explainable and Feature-Engineered Machine Learning for Stock Market Forecasting: A Survey of Lexicon-Based, Statistical, and Sentiment-Driven Approaches
authors: Sidharth S; Harichandana H S; Albin Tom Thomas; Akhilesh P A; Mrs. Sagara M R
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
abstract: Forecasting the direction and magnitude of stock price movements remains one of the most persistently difficult problems in applied machine learning, owing to the noisy, non-stationary, and weak-form-efficient character of financial time series. This survey examines three recent studies that approach the problem through complementary lenses: an explainable Decision Tree that builds dynamic, industry-specific lexicons from financial news to classify next-day price-change magnitude [1]; a feature-engineering and portfolio-construction pipeline that derives new price-based predictors via Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and a proposed Statistical Average Method (SAM) before applying eight regression architectures, including Bi-LSTM [2]; and an LSTM-based trend classifier that fuses FinBERT-scored Twitter sentiment with price data to forecast North American and European bank-stock movements during the macroeconomically turbulent year of 2022 [3]. Beyond summarising each study's objectives, methodology, data, and results, this survey situates the three works within the broader and rapidly evolving literature on deep sequence models (LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU, and transformer architectures), sentiment analysis with pretrained financial language models such as FinBERT, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in finance. A structured comparative analysis contrasts the three studies along ten dimensions, including data sources, feature engineering, model architecture, explainability, validation design, and reported performance, while explicitly cautioning against directly ranking studies whose prediction tasks and evaluation metrics are not commensurable. A cross-domain case study of an attention-based legislative-vote predictor is retained to examine whether a learned similarity mechanism could improve on the fixed similarity rules used throughout the finance literature reviewed here. The survey's contribution lies in bringing explainable lexicon-based methods, statistically engineered price features, and sentiment-driven deep learning together within a single comparative framework, and in using that synthesis to identify concrete, evidence-grounded gaps around auxiliary-signal fusion, the explainability of high-accuracy sequence models, and cross-market generalisation.

title: MiDashengLM-Spatial: Unifying General Audio Understanding and Spatial Awareness
authors: Jinbo Hu; Hang Su; Lichun Fan; Heinrich Dinkel; Gang Li; Zhanchen Dai; Yiru Zhang; Chang Liu; Peng Wang; Junnan Wu; Jian Luan; Cong Zou; Heng Qu
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance in general audio understanding, yet most are designed for monaural input and discard the inter-channel cues essential for spatial perception. In contrast, existing spatial audio-language models are purpose-built for spatial tasks and fail to capitalize on the general understanding capabilities of monaural LALMs. We present MiDashengLM-Spatial, the first open-source end-to-end unified audio-language model, to our knowledge, which supports both general audio understanding and spatial awareness within a single architecture. It extends MiDashengLM with a spatial audio encoder, Spatial-Dasheng, integrated through a hierarchical semantic-to-spatial conditioning module that injects intermediate semantic representations into the spatial branch at multiple depths while preserving the original semantic pathway. To provide spatial audio-language supervision at scale, we develop a data synthesis pipeline that renders diverse spatial acoustic scenes with scene-level spatial descriptions and question-answer pairs. Experiments show that Spatial-Dasheng achieves strong performance on sound event localization and detection in real-world scenes, and that MiDashengLM-Spatial substantially outperforms existing LALMs on spatial understanding and reasoning benchmarks. Meanwhile, it remains competitive with state-of-the-art 8B-scale LALMs on diverse monaural benchmarks, demonstrating that spatial awareness can be acquired without compromising general audio understanding. The source code and model checkpoint are available at https://github.com/xiaomi-research/midashenglm-spatial and https://huggingface.co/mispeech/midashenglm-spatial.

title: Visual-Invariance-Augmented Feature Optimal Alignment for Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Closed-Source MLLMs
authors: Xiaojun Jia; Simeng Qin; Yiming Li; Jie Liao; Sensen Gao; Ke Ma; Yang Liu; Xiaochun Cao
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remain vulnerable to transferable adversarial examples, especially in black-box settings where only open-source surrogate models are accessible. Existing targeted transfer attacks mainly align adversarial and target samples using global image-level features, such as encoder [CLS] embeddings. However, such coarse alignment insufficiently exploits patch-level visual structures, limiting transferability across heterogeneous closed-source MLLMs. We propose IAU-FOA, a visual-invariance-augmented feature optimal alignment attack with adaptive unbalanced transport, to improve targeted transferability against closed-source MLLMs. IAU-FOA aligns adversarial and target samples at both global and local levels: a cosine-based objective narrows their global semantic gap, while patch tokens are clustered into compact local patterns and matched through optimal transport for fine-grained feature alignment. Balanced optimal transport enforces fixed marginal masses even for local clusters without reliable counterparts, potentially introducing misleading alignment gradients. We therefore introduce confidence-adaptive unbalanced transport to relax these constraints for weakly matched clusters, aiming to reduce unreliable local alignment and improve adversarial transferability. We further study the effect of input transformations and propose visual-invariance augmentation, which applies bidirectional pixel-intensity rescaling and per-channel white-balance adjustment to simulate exposure, contrast, illumination, and color-temperature variations. This strategy encourages adversarial perturbations to generalize across different visual encoders. Extensive experiments on open-source and closed-source MLLMs show that IAU-FOA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art transferable attack methods. Code is available at https://github.com/jiaxiaojunQAQ/IAU-FOA.

title: ThyCLIPNet: A BiomedCLIP-Guided Lightweight Attention-Enhanced DeepLabV3+ Framework for Robust Thyroid Nodule Segmentation
authors: Tasnim Jahan; Md Easin Arafat; Swakkhar Shatabda
abstract: Accurate thyroid ultrasound segmentation is often challenged by low contrast, speckle noise, and unclear boundaries. Although recent methods have improved segmentation accuracy, many rely on resource-intensive architectures or lack explicit integration of multiscale features with global biomedical visual guidance. In this paper, we introduce ThyCLIPNet, a lightweight semantic-guided hybrid encoder-decoder framework that integrates BiomedCLIP-derived biomedical semantic guidance into a lightweight multi-scale CNN segmentation pipeline. The encoder integrates MobileNetV2 with efficient channel attention, while atrous spatial pyramid pooling and a custom convolutional block attention module enrich bottleneck features. The decoder combines hierarchical skip connections and lightweight attention refinement with a BiomedCLIP-guided gated fusion pathway that projects vision-only global biomedical embeddings into decoder feature space and selectively integrates them through semantic-local fusion and spatial gating. To the best of our knowledge, ThyCLIPNet is among the first lightweight thyroid ultrasound segmentation frameworks to use BiomedCLIP's vision encoder alone for image-only global semantic guidance without text prompting. Experiments on TG3K, TN3K, DDTI, and PKTN achieve dice similarity coefficients of 96.22%, 87.58%, 84.73%, and 80.70%; intersection over union scores of 92.72%, 77.91%, 73.51%, and 67.64%; and 95th-percentile hausdorff distances of 3.75, 16.38, 18.23, and 10.86, respectively. ThyCLIPNet uses 8.55M parameters and 22.99G FLOPs. Overall, the results support integrating global biomedical semantic guidance with lightweight multi-scale CNN representations for robust and computationally efficient thyroid ultrasound segmentation. Source code: https://github.com/Tasnim-Jahan/ThyCLIPNet. [Abstract shortened for arXiv. See PDF for full abstract.]

title: PhaseAT: Fourier Phase Adversarial Training for Medical Image Domain Generalization
authors: Ahmed Sharshar; Asif Hanif; Naveen Kumar Kummari; Mohammad Yaqub; Mohsen Guizan
abstract: Reliable clinical deployment of deep medical image models is hindered by distribution shifts across scanners, sites, and acquisition protocols. Existing domain generalization (DG) methods often focus on style or intensity diversification, but they can still leave networks dependent on domain-specific texture correlations. Inspired by evidence that Fourier phase encodes semantic structure, we introduce PhaseAT, a phase-aware adversarial training framework for medical DG. PhaseAT forms phase-perturbed training views in the Fourier domain by iteratively updating a bounded phase perturbation while keeping the amplitude spectrum unchanged, thereby stressing spatial organization under matched appearance statistics. Perturbations are applied only to the luminance channel in YCbCr color space to avoid chromatic artifacts. Additionally, a simple phase-saliency mask concentrates updates on the most influential frequencies. The model is trained with a weighted combination of losses on clean and phase-perturbed samples, supporting both single-source and multi-source DG. We validate our method on two challenging medical datasets and demonstrate that PhaseAT achieves over 20% improvement in single-source domain generalization, outperforming several state-of-the-art DG methods. The code implementation is available at: https://github.com/ahmed-sharshar/PhaseAT.

title: Semantic-Aware Joint Source-Channel Optimization for Encoder-Agnostic Digital Video Communication
authors: Xiangben Zhu; Caili Guo; Yang Yang; Chuanhong Liu; Meiyi Zhu
abstract: Video semantic communication has attracted increasing attention as a promising approach to improving video transmission efficiency. However, most existing approaches rely on computationally intensive deep learning-based video encoders and decoders, which hinders their deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight semantic-aware joint source-channel optimization (SAJSCO) scheme that can be integrated into existing digital video communication systems as a plug-in module. Specifically, we develop a video communication system model in which the transmitter jointly optimizes source and channel coding parameters based on the inter-frame semantic importance of the input video and estimated channel state information. On this basis, we formulate an optimization problem that maximizes semantic importance weighted video reconstruction quality under a maximum bitrate constraint. To solve it, we first quantify inter-frame semantic importance using a cosine similarity-based metric with a shifted window mechanism. We then develop a multi-actor proximal policy optimization (MPPO) algorithm to solve the formulated problem by jointly adapting the source compression rate and channel coding rate. The learned policy can be directly applied to different video encoders without encoder-specific retraining or fine-tuning. SAJSCO achieves Bjøntegaard Delta rate reductions of 34.86\% and 18.01\% when integrated with H.265, a conventional video encoder, and DCVC-RT, a deep learning-based video encoder. Over-the-air experiments on a hardware testbed further demonstrate a PSNR gain of up to 1.448 dB with H.265 and an LPIPS reduction of up to 0.033 with DCVC-RT compared with the respective best-performing fixed-parameter baselines.

title: End-to-End Optical Semantic Communication over a Nonlinear WDM Fiber Link
authors: Hussein Jammal; Andrea Bianco; Cristina Rottondi
abstract: Emerging optical-network applications increasingly use received data for inference and control rather than exact source reproduction, creating an opportunity to trade bit-level fidelity for greater transmission reach and efficiency. We propose an end-to-end optical semantic communication system for joint image classification and reconstruction over a nonlinear wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) fiber channel. The system maps each image directly into a fixed-length sequence of channel symbols that preserves task-relevant information, without explicit source compression or channel coding. Experiments on the MNIST dataset cover launch powers from -9 to +3 dBm, fiber lengths up to 800 km, and 16-, 64-, and 256-Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) formats. At 0 dBm, classification accuracy remains between 98.92% and 99.31% across all tested link lengths and modulation orders, while requiring fewer transmitted symbols than a Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC)-coded JPEG baseline at every tested modulation order. These results show that semantic communication can simultaneously extend optical reach and reduce transmission resources by conveying only task-relevant information.

title: Dual-Branch Vector-Quantization-Aided Satellite Digital Semantic Communication with Index Compression for High-Resolution RSI Over AFDM
authors: Jianqiao Chen; Nan Ma; Xiaodong Xu; Tingting Zhu; Huishi Song; Chen Dong; Rui Meng; Wenkai Liu; Ke Peng; Ping Zhang
abstract: High-resolution remote sensing imagery (RSI) transmission is constrained by satellite-ground bandwidth and channel impairments, yet existing methods struggle to simultaneously achieve extreme compression and robust transmission. To address this, we propose a dual-branch vector-quantization aided satellite digital semantic communication (DVQ-SDSC) framework for RSI transmission over affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), whose bandwidth savings arise from two interrelated aspects. First, at the source-coding level, a dual-branch framework is developed to unify deep joint semantic coding, VQ-aided index transmission, channel estimation and adaption in an end-to-end architecture; departing from symmetric encoder designs, the codec is recast as an asymmetric dual-branch architecture that separately processes the high-frequency residuals and the low-frequency structural semantics, with gated fusion and channel-adaptive reconstruction jointly restoring the semantic content. Second, at the index-coding level, we develop a principal component analysis (PCA)-aided codebook reordering to align index topology with latent correlations, and devise group differential pulse-code modulation (G-DPCM) to encode prediction residuals rather than absolute indices, lowering the index bitrate while locally isolating clipping and channel errors. A two-stage training strategy further decouples channel impairments from the semantic codec. FAIR1M experiments over 3GPP NTN-TDL-D demonstrate that DVQ-SDSC with G-DPCM index coding outperforms the conventional JPEG-LDPC scheme at the base rate of 0.0625 bits per pixel (BPP), and that G-DPCM applies directly to the trained codec without retraining, yielding additional index compression at no extra cost.

title: Representation-Dependent Recoverability in Quantum Compilation
authors: Jinze Yang; Yangyang Li; Xiu-Hao Deng
abstract: Fault-tolerant compilation can disperse high-level structure: schedules split an accumulated phase across rounds, gate synthesis replaces an angle by a Clifford+$T$ word, and randomized compiling spreads rotations over sign-randomized fragments. They preserve the computation but change how cheaply a downstream compiler can recover the aggregate phase data. We formalize this representation-dependent recoverability by charging two channels: output committed before the suffix arrives, and a serialized restart state crossing the cut. For an $r$-round accumulation of a commuting layer with $m$ generators at accuracy $ε$ ($K_ε=Θ(1/ε)$), any $p$-pass compiler correct on every valid stream with failure probability at most $δ$ obeys $\overline{A}_p+(2p-1)S\geq(1-δ)m\log_2 K_ε-h_2(δ)$, where $\overline{A}_p$ is committed output and $S$ is the crossing-state cap. The bound covers compile-time randomized compiling; a memory-capped block compiler attains it within a constant factor, and direct semantic aggregation reaches compact output with logarithmic state. The two channels are not always interchangeable. A compiler whose committed prefix is executed at the cut pays a toll the state channel never pays: the entropy $\log_2\binom{m}{k}$ of the mask naming which $k$ coordinates it commits early. Compilers that defer or buffer pay none of it. We prove both directions and, with instrumented compilers under a preregistered protocol, measure a per-generator toll matching $\log_2\binom{m}{k}/k$ that vanishes for a public mask and a buffered control. Under a disclosed fixed-total-error Clifford+$T$ and surface-code model, a materialize-first pipeline costs orders of magnitude more logical $T$ states and spacetime volume than a semantic-first one. Phase semantics should therefore be preserved until aggregation whenever the interface permits.

title: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset
authors: Mohammad Abolnejadian; Matthew Brehmer
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset 📄 Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3830398.3830522💻 Code: https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast Supplemental dataset for the paper: InsightToast: Proactive Information Retrieval & Glanceable Visualization in the Side Channel of Data-Rich Meetings Mohammad Abolnejadian and Matthew Brehmer. Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '26). DOI: 10.1145/3830398.3830522 This dataset provides a collection of 43,878 open legislative records from the Canadian House of Commons, spanning 1994 to 2025, covering document types such as debates (Hansard), legislative bills, committee reports, petitions, recorded votes, order papers, and Library of Parliament research publications. It is released at three stages of the same pipeline: the raw collected documents, a processed corpus that has been passed through an ETL pipeline and chunked for use in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, and an embedded, pre-indexed vector store built from that processed corpus. The dataset supports the development and user study of the InsightToast project. The embedded form can be placed directly into the project's codebase, open sourced at https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast, where it serves as the knowledge base when InsightToast operates as a proactive side-channel assistant in policy discussion meetings. Usage in the InsightToast Backend Only qdrant_storage.tar.gz is required to run the backend. Extract it into the root of the InsightToast project, so that qdrant_storage/ sits alongside docker-compose.yml, and start the services: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz -C /path/to/InsightToast/ cd /path/to/InsightToast docker compose up --build -d Contents File What it is Approx. size parliament_data.tar.gz Raw source corpus of 43,878 parliamentary records, as 57,124 files (.txt + .pdf) 8.1 GB compressed / 11 GB extracted parliament_data_processed.tar.gz Processed corpus: the same records cleaned, normalized, and chunked into RAG-ready JSON 2.1 GB compressed / 9.1 GB extracted qdrant_storage.tar.gz Pre-indexed Qdrant vector store, ready to mount as the knowledge base 21 GB compressed / 27 GB extracted parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the raw corpus, viewable without downloading the archive small parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the processed corpus small qdrant_storage.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the vector store small SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums for the three archives small Verify the archives after download: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt Source Corpus: Raw Parliamentary Documents parliament_data.tar.gz contains open legislative documents collected across the range of record types produced by the Canadian House of Commons and the Library of Parliament, including the proceedings of debate, the texts of bills as tabled, the reports of standing committees, the petitions presented to the House, and the recorded outcomes of divisions. The documents were assembled from three public sources: the House of Commons (ourcommons.ca, including the Legislative Information service, LEGISinfo), the Library of Parliament of Canada (parl-gc.primo.exlibrisgroup.com), and the independent open-data mirror openparliament.ca. No private, personal, or access-restricted material is included; Member of Parliament profiles contain only information published in an official public capacity. Total: 43,878 parliamentary records, distributed across 57,124 files (43,634 .txt + 13,490 .pdf). Each record is provided as extracted plain text, with the source PDF alongside it under the same basename where one exists, so records that carry both formats account for two files. Temporal coverage: documents span the 35th through 45th Parliaments. Debates run from 1994-01-17 to 2025-10-10; coverage of the other record types varies by type. Languages: the source records are bilingual (English and French), as published by Parliament. Filename conventions: debates use sitting dates (YYYY-MM-DD- .txt); bills, journals, order papers, and votes use - - (for example, 37-1-C-10); petitions and Library of Parliament publications use slugified titles. Category Files Description debates/ 18,347 House of Commons debates (Hansard transcripts), one file per sitting day bills/ 10,561 Legislative bills, full text plus the original tabled PDF journals/ 7,038 Official Journals of the House (daily record of decisions) petitions/ 6,093 e-Petitions and paper petitions presented to the House votes/ 4,521 Recorded division and vote results order-papers/ 4,228 Order Paper and Notice Paper (daily agenda) library/ 2,202 Library of Parliament publications and tabled agreements committee-reports/ 1,577 Standing and joint committee reports, grouped into 27 committee subfolders politicians/ 1,319 Member of Parliament profiles research/ 1,210 Library of Parliament research and HillNotes publications committees/ 28 Committee mandate and description summaries Total 57,124 See parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt for the full breakdown, including all committee subfolders. Processed Corpus: Cleaned and Chunked Records parliament_data_processed.tar.gz contains the same corpus after the ETL pipeline that turns each document into retrievable units. Documents are parsed from their metadata header and routed by document_type. Bilingual records are language-identified with langdetect and reduced to their English content by an LLM pass. PDFs are structurally partitioned with unstructured's partition_pdf into text, table, and image elements; table elements are linearized into prose by an LLM, and salient figures are captioned, written to images/, and linked from their chunk via has_images. Records whose content is inherently tabular, namely recorded votes, petitions, and Member profiles, are rendered into natural-language narratives to keep them semantically retrievable rather than reducing to fields. Type-specific pre-segmentation then splits debates on speaker turns, preserving the speaker, section, and timestamp, before every stream passes through a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (1,000 characters, 200 overlap); each resulting chunk is tagged with its content_type (text, table, or image) and its provenance. The output is one JSON document per record, holding the record's metadata and its ordered list of chunks: { "metadata": { "document_type": "debate", "session": "35-1", "date": "1994-01-17", "language": "en", "source_file": "debates/1994-01-17-1.txt", "source_url": "...", "total_chunks": 51 }, "chunks": [ { "chunk_id": 0, "content": "...", "metadata": { "speaker": "...", "section": "...", "content_type": "text", "has_images": false } } ] } Volume: 42,014 JSON records and 2,170 extracted images, totaling 6,379,732 chunks, which is the set embedded into the knowledge base below. Traceability: every record's metadata.source_file links back to its file in the raw corpus. Coverage: most record types are processed in full; committee-report and library are present as subsets of the raw corpus. See parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt for per-category counts. Indexed Knowledge Base qdrant_storage.tar.gz contains the processed corpus above embedded and indexed into Qdrant, ready to serve as the retrieval backend with no further processing. title: Test-time optimization for domain adaptive open vocabulary segmentation
authors: Ulindu De Silva; Didula Samaraweera; Sasini Wanigathunga; K.B.G.L.W. Kariyawasam; Kanchana Ranasinghe; Muzammal Naseer; Ranga P. Rodrigo
abstract: We present Seg-TTO, a novel framework for zero-shot, open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS), designed to excel in specialized domain tasks. While current open-vocabulary approaches show impressive performance on standard segmentation benchmarks under zero-shot settings, they fall short of supervised counterparts on highly domain-specific datasets. We focus on segmentation-specific test-time optimization to address this gap. Segmentation requires an understanding of multiple concepts within a single image while retaining the locality and spatial structure of representations. We propose a novel self-supervised objective adhering to these requirements and use it to align the model parameters with input images at test time. In the textual modality, we learn multiple embeddings for each category to capture diverse concepts within an image, while in the visual modality, we calculate pixel-level losses followed by embedding aggregation operations specific to preserving spatial structure. Every pretrained backbone, vision-language encoder and decoder weight stays frozen, no training or target-domain data is used, and no adapted state is carried from one test image to the next. Our resulting framework termed Seg-TTO is a plug-and-play module. We integrate Seg-TTO with state-of-the-art OVSS approaches (CAT-Seg and CLIP-DINOiser, spanning three model variants) and evaluate across 22 challenging OVSS tasks from the MESS benchmark, covering a range of specialized domains. Our Seg-TTO demonstrates clear performance improvements, with mean gains of 1.8, 2.6 and 1.6 mIoU over CAT-Seg-B, CAT-Seg-L and CLIP-DINOiser respectively, improving on 20 of the 22 datasets for both CAT-Seg variants, with relative improvements of up to 57% and 27% on individual specialized-domain datasets for CAT-Seg-B and CAT-Seg-L respectively, establishing new state-of-the-art. Our code, the exact LLM-generated attribute sets, and models will be released publicly.
